constraints: Read-only: it rewrites nothing and writes only the optional --json file. It is a CANDIDATE screen, never a licence to author a rule — the Mandatory-policy source-exhaustion bar still applies to every rule it suggests.

Pairs words at the SAME BYTE OFFSET, so it OVER-reports on schedule-class functions (fabricating pairs out of two differently-ordered streams) and UNDER-reports any member displaced by a schedule difference. A zero result means 'no member at a fixed offset', never 'no member'.
Only equal-size function pairs are screened; a count-asymmetric residual is outside every postprocessor class by construction.

Founding run 2026-09-01 over 326 target objects: 1 strict member (game/movie/movieplayer::fn_800D87FC, closed) and 1 ADJACENT hit that fndiff --ops confirmed was a pure reorder, i.e. a false positive.
name: wf_range_proof_census.py
purpose: Image-wide screen for members of the WebFrank range-proof class (redundant rlwinm mask bits), reporting each candidate's obligation, whether the class's own prover discharges it, and how many other differing words remain.
usage: Run from the repository root after a completed `ninja` — it joins build/GUNE5D/obj (the extracted target) against the RAW pre-WebFrank bodies under build/GUNE5D/src/**/.postprocess/body, falling back to the plain object for units with no WebFrank rules, so it scores compiler output and not postprocessed output.

Read the `remaining` column: 0 with proved>0 means the class closes the function ALONE; proved>0 with remaining>0 means the class unblocks a composition that still needs the permutation and/or recolor stages, which is what fn_800D87FC turned out to be.

Confirm every hit with `fndiff --ops` before counting it — see the ADJACENT false positive recorded in claim.law.WF_range-proof-population-is-one-and-offset-paired-censuses-lie-in-both-directions.20260901.v1.
